# Test fixtures

The `.nc` files here are generated from the CDL sources in `cdl/` by
netCDF-C's `ncgen`, and their `ncdump` output is kept in `ncdump/` as the
reference the Go tests compare against. They are small (a few hundred bytes
each) and are committed deliberately.

## Oracle

- netCDF-C **v4.10.1**, pin `ad3d53827` (2026-07-09), from the netCDF-C repository.
- Built in WSL from that source with m4 and zlib extracted without root:

  ```sh
  ./configure --disable-hdf5 --disable-dap --disable-nczarr \
      --disable-shared --disable-libxml2
  make -j2
  ```

  That build is classic-only: `ncgen` refuses CDL that needs the enhanced
  data model (`--disable-hdf5` removes it), so the CDF-5 fixture carries only
  the six classic types. The CDF-5 unsigned and 64-bit types are covered by
  the hand-built fixtures in `internal/cdf/header_test.go`; once the writer
  exists, `ncdump` reading our own CDF-5 output covers them against C.

## Regenerating

From the build directory, with `REPO` pointing at this repository root:

```sh
gen() {
  name=$1; k=$2
  ./ncgen/ncgen -k "$k" -o "out/${name}-cdf${k}.nc" "$REPO/testdata/cdl/${name}.cdl"
  ./ncdump/ncdump -h "out/${name}-cdf${k}.nc" > "out/${name}-cdf${k}.h.txt"
  ./ncdump/ncdump "out/${name}-cdf${k}.nc" > "out/${name}-cdf${k}.dump.txt"
}
gen simple 1 ; gen simple 2 ; gen simple 5
gen types 1 ; gen types 2
gen record 1 ; gen record 2 ; gen record 5
gen layout 1 ; gen layout 2 ; gen layout 5
gen fill 1 ; gen fill 2 ; gen fill 5
gen single_rec 1
gen empty 1
gen attrs 1
```

Copy `out/*.nc` to `testdata/` and `out/*.txt` to `testdata/ncdump/`.

## What each fixture covers

| Fixture | Covers |
|---|---|
| `simple-cdf{1,2,5}.nc` | two dimensions, fixed variables, global and variable attributes of char, int and double type, all three formats |
| `types-cdf{1,2}.nc` | every classic type, both 32-bit and 64-bit offset headers |
| `record-cdf{1,2,5}.nc` | unlimited dimension, record variables of different types and widths, interleaved records, a fixed variable before the record section |
| `layout-cdf{1,2,5}.nc` | a 3-D fixed variable and a byte record variable beside an int record variable (the record padding path); every sub-slab of both is checked against a full read |
| `fill-cdf{1,2,5}.nc` | variables declared without data: the file holds only the initial fill of every type, which is what the writer's `FillFixed` must reproduce byte for byte |
| `cdf5types-cdf5.nc` | the five CDF-5-only types (ubyte, ushort, uint, int64, uint64); the writer's own output, kept byte for byte as a regression fixture (see below) |
| `single_rec-cdf1.nc` | the specification's special case: one record variable, no padding between records |
| `empty-cdf1.nc` | a file with no dimensions, attributes or variables (netCDF-C pads it to 4096 bytes) |
| `attrs-cdf1.nc` | attribute types and a variable attribute list |

`cdl/cdf5.cdl` documents the intended CDF-5 type coverage but cannot be
generated by the classic-only oracle build; see the note above. The CDF-5
five-type file is therefore the writer's own output, and its evidence comes
from two sides:

- `ncdump/cdf5types-cdf5.dump.txt` — `ncdump` reading that file (the oracle
  check), kept as the human-readable reference;
- `cdf5types-cdf5.nc` — the same bytes committed as a fixture, so
  `TestCreateMatchesFixtures` fails if the CDF-5 encoding regresses. The
  generator is tracked:

  ```sh
  go run testdata/gen/cdf5types.go testdata/cdf5types-cdf5.nc
  /tmp/ncbuild/src/ncdump/ncdump testdata/cdf5types-cdf5.nc \
      > testdata/ncdump/cdf5types-cdf5.dump.txt
  ```

A regenerated fixture makes the test pass by construction — check the diff
before committing it; the committed `ncdump` dump is what proves the values.

The initial fill is compared with the oracle through `fill-cdf*`; record
extension fill cannot be expressed in CDL, so it was validated by a manual
probe against netCDF-C 4.10.1.

## Oracle corpus (differential harness)

`oracle/cdl/` holds nine CDL models copied unchanged from netCDF-C's `nc_test/` at the
same pin. The `//go:build oracle` harness (`oracle_corpus_test.go`) generates every model
for CDF-1, CDF-2 and CDF-5, reads it with our reader, writes it back with our writer, and
compares the `ncdump` text of both files (full precision, same dataset name); `nccopy -k`
then converts both to another kind and the converted texts are compared too.

Run it where the reference tools are present:

```sh
go test -tags oracle -run TestOracle -v ./...            # ncgen, ncdump, nccopy on PATH
NETCDF_ORACLE_BIN=/path/to/one/dir go test -tags oracle -run TestOracle -v ./...
```

`NETCDF_ORACLE_BIN` names one directory that holds all three tools; the WSL classic build
keeps them in two, so prepend both to `PATH`:

```sh
PATH=/tmp/ncbuild/src/ncgen:/tmp/ncbuild/src/ncdump:$PATH \
    go test -tags oracle -run TestOracle -v ./...
```

With the tag set a missing tool fails the test — it never skips. CI runs the same command
in the `Oracle - netCDF-C tools` job.

Two upstream models are not in the corpus: `ref_tst_diskless2.cdl` uses the enhanced data
model (enum, opaque, vlen, string) and `ref_tst_http_nc4b.cdl` uses two unlimited
dimensions; neither is expressible in the classic formats. `ref_tst_http_nc4e.cdl` is
byte-identical to `ref_tst_http_nc4a.cdl` and is not duplicated.

## Files taken from the netCDF-C test corpus

Four files are copied unchanged from the same pin. netCDF-C is distributed
under the BSD 3-Clause licence; its notice travels with them in
[`LICENSE-netcdf-c`](LICENSE-netcdf-c).

| File | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `nctest_names-cdf1.nc` (source: `nctest/ref_nctest_classic.nc`) | names whose declared length runs into NUL bytes (`yy`, `pp`, `plugh`); netCDF-C reads them trimmed at the first NUL |
| `nctest_names-cdf2.nc` (source: `nctest/ref_nctest_64bit_offset.nc`) | the same model in CDF-2 |
| `null_byte_padding-cdf2.nc` (source: `ncdump/ref_null_byte_padding_test.nc`) | a CDF-2 file whose header padding is not NUL bytes; netCDF-C accepts it, so the reader must too |
| `bad_cdf5_begin.nc` (source: `nc_test/bad_cdf5_begin.nc`) | a deliberately corrupt CDF-5 file that netCDF-C rejects; the reader must reject it as well |

The copies are byte-identical to their sources (checked with `sha256sum` when
they were added, 2026-11-14).

Their `ncdump` output is in `ncdump/`; `bad_cdf5_begin.nc` has no dump because
`ncdump` refuses it.
